slice: exploring: entraining and co-sequencing orientings from many directions

items.section: 4.6 The gather has half the competency and all the increase
items.sentence: And a gathering is local and immediate.
items.text: A bacterium is swimming in runs of about a second each, comparing the attractant of its last second with the three seconds before; a run going up the gradient is lengthening, and after each tumbling its new heading is leaning forward, about 62 degrees from its prior heading.

items.section: 2.3 Co-unrelationing, one and then the other
items.sentence: Co-unrelationing, one and then the other, discovers, frees, discovers a fixing its discovery lands, frees again, going on.
items.text: A male moth meeting a scent plume is surging upwind, and losing the scent it is casting crosswind until meeting it again, one and then the other; ahead of first meeting, its searching is going in long and short paths in changing directions.

items.section: 1.1 In disequilibria, changing and changing back is a stable-forming method
items.sentence: Neither by itself is living: a discovering ungathering scatters and a gathering undiscovering folds, so a living method is their changing and changing back.
items.text: A growing climbing-plant tip is sweeping in circles, its growing making the circles a spiral; it is sweeping wide circles until touching a support, and then its circles are tightening and it is winding around the support as it grows, a reaching and a gathering one and then the other.

items.sentence: A self discovers by un-relating its own fixings; selves discover together by un-relating fixings between them, co-competencing, a same-existing-society co-chaining one same method a self co-chains by itself.
items.text: A synchronous firefly seeing a partner's flashing is pausing for 3.0 to 24.1 seconds and opening again flashing at one with its partner; alone and shown rhythmic light, it is pausing and opening with its first flash locking to the light at a small delay, each firefly entraining through its own pausing and opening.

items.sentence: A same-existing-society co-chains a method between selves, un-relating two-way, each self pacing its own time and abundancing in no self alone.
items.text: A bird in a flock of a few thousand is interacting with about six or seven nearest birds, the same number however near or far they are, and with this number the flock is holding whole through sharp changes of crowding.

items.sentence: Geodesic discovery is co-unrelationing co-chaining a straightest un-relating, free-moving, adding nothing, relating showing where fixings free of themselves.
items.text: Ants between nest and food over a bridge of two branches, one shorter, are opening about half on each; ants on the shorter branch are coming back sooner and marking it sooner, ants going out are leaning to the branch with more trail, and nearly the whole colony comes to the shorter branch, with no ant holding the bridge whole.

Orientings from many directions are clustering five ways: a self keeping on while its now is changing for better beside its prior and turning as it is changing back (a bacterium, a sperm, a moth, a zebrafish); a self orienting by its own winding (a sperm's helix, a plant tip's circling, a honeybee summing its image motion); a self orienting by a not-changing beyond it (star points, the Milky Way, swells); selves entraining with each other (fireflies, six or seven birds, water striders' waves); and a society co-chaining its geodesic with no self holding it whole (ants).

Natural illustrations of orienting from within a surface: a canoe as its own side with islands sliding back beneath star points; a sperm's helix bending toward rising and turning sharply at falling; a plant tip circling wide and tightening around a support; fireflies pausing and opening at one; ants coming to the shorter of two branches; a bird with its six or seven; each drawing a self orienting by a parity of now beside its prior.

One orienting is coming from each direction of living, a bacterium, a sperm, a plant tip, an insect, a fish, a bird, an ocean wayfinder and an ant colony: each self orienting from its own side by a parity of now beside its prior, entraining with its others and co-sequencing its going on, a universal method of unrelationing with no map and no measure apart.
